criteria.criterion: defaults.toml has a [[default]] with id "root-cause", source "BRIEF.md 2026-10-13: Root causes", and applies_to ["*"] or a justified list.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, defaults.toml gains a [[default]] entry with id = "root-cause", applies_to = ["*"] and source = "BRIEF.md 2026-10-13: Root causes". That source matches the BRIEF.md heading at line 498.

criteria.criterion: The statement covers: fix where the fault originates, not the symptom or one instance; name an out-of-scope cause and propose the fix rather than working around it; the fix's description names the root cause and why the change addresses it.
criteria.evidence: The statement is: "Fix a fault at its origin, not its symptom. Report an out-of-scope cause with a proposed fix; don't work around it. The description names the cause. The root-cause fix is the one small change." It covers fixing at the origin rather than the symptom, and reporting an out-of-scope cause with a proposed fix. It does not cover 'not one instance'. It also does not cover 'why the change addresses it': the description only has to name the cause.

criteria.criterion: The statement says how it relates to 'small': the root-cause fix is the one focused change, and an out-of-scope cause is reported, not fixed.
criteria.evidence: The statement says "The root-cause fix is the one small change." and "Report an out-of-scope cause with a proposed fix". Reporting with a proposed fix implies the cause is not fixed in this change, although the statement never says so outright.

criteria.criterion: The entry is short (about 400 bytes of statement or less). BRIEF.md and the budget constants are unchanged.
criteria.evidence: The statement is about 190 bytes (counted from the diff text). The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, reader.md and defaults.toml, so BRIEF.md and the budget code are unchanged.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`: every test passes, including budgets::every_role_set_is_within_its_budget (reader set at or under 1800 tokens).
criteria.evidence: The budgets test printed "estimated tokens: reader 1799, ..." and every_role_set_is_within_its_budget passed. The full suite passed with 0 failures; some tests are ignored, the same tests that are ignored on the base tree.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Both commands exited 0 with no warnings or diffs.

findings.summary: The root-cause statement drops two parts of the required meaning: 'not one instance' and 'why the change addresses it'.
findings.evidence: The statement says "not its symptom" and "The description names the cause." Criterion 2 also requires 'not ... one instance' and that the description says why the change addresses the cause. The user asked to keep the same meaning. With the reader set at 1799/1800 tokens, adding these phrases will need further trims in reader.md.

findings.summary: One reader-prompt trim slightly changes meaning: 'the owner's private files' became 'private files'.
findings.evidence: The diff changes "records/, the owner's private files, and history are absent by design" to "records/, private files, and history are absent". The new wording no longer says whose private files are excluded.

findings.summary: The statement says 'The description' without saying whose description.
findings.evidence: "The description names the cause." A reader has to infer that it means the change's or PR's description.

summary: The candidate adds a short 'root-cause' default (about 190 bytes) to defaults.toml and trims the reader prompt. I ran the budgets test and it reports the reader set at 1799 tokens against a budget of 1800, so it fits. The full `cargo test --locked`, clippy and fmt all pass. BRIEF.md and the budget constants are unchanged. However, the entry leaves out two things criterion 2 asks for by name. It never says to fix the fault itself rather than one instance of it. It says the description names the cause, but not why the change addresses that cause. The user asked for the same meaning in fewer words, so this is a major finding and the verdict is fail. The reader set has only 1 token of slack left, so restoring those phrases will need a little more trimming of the reader prompt. Leaving the budget alone means that trimming is the only option.
